name: Nine Entertainment Vulnerability Disclosure Program
notes:
Scope + full exclusions populated 2026-08-05 from the authenticated Bugcrowd brief. VDP = disclosure only, non-monetary; Bugcrowd VRT.

*** CRITICAL: THE PROGRAM PROHIBITS 'No automated scanning'. ***
bb-beast is an automated scanner, so its ACTIVE pipeline (httpx probing, nuclei, ffuf/feroxbuster, katana, dalfox, sqlmap, and the validator's probe loop) MUST NOT be run against this program. allowed_test_types is deliberately set to ['recon'] ONLY, so the validator scope gate BLOCKS every active test type (xss/sqli/ssrf/etc.) — fail-closed by design. Use this program for PASSIVE recon (third-party OSINT/subdomain data that does not touch Nine infra) and MANUAL testing only. Every finding requires a manual proof-of-concept; the program rejects 'generic vulnerability scan results without proof of concept'.

HARD PROHIBITIONS (out_of_scope.test_types): automated scanning; volume/DoS/DDoS/brute force/rate-limiting; attacks on customers/end users; use of stolen/breached credentials; modifying/deleting/retaining Nine or customer data; social engineering/phishing/physical; post-exploitation unless explicitly approved; attacks on third-party services (LinkedIn/Twitter/etc.).

WON'T-ACCEPT NOISE (deprioritize in triage, don't report): outdated-browser issues; cookie flags (Secure/HTTPOnly); missing/misconfigured security headers (CSP/HSTS/X-XSS-Protection/Cache-Control); clickjacking / missing X-Frame-Options; email config (SPF/DKIM/DMARC); verbose errors/stack traces/status codes; functional/UI/UX/spelling bugs; non-exploitable config (weak TLS ciphers, password policy, session expiry, cert pinning, version-disclosing headers); non-sensitive exposed API keys (Google Maps, Raygun).

OPERATIONAL: do NOT submit contact forms / create tickets / send emails that generate work for non-security staff. Use an @bugcrowdninja.com email for any research that needs one. Personal credentials (your own or discovered) are allowed for testing. OUT-OF-SCOPE domains: *.domain.com.au (Domain Group), businessinsider.com.au. The brief also broadly authorizes 'Any Nine owned asset' beyond the enumerated list — confirm Nine ownership before touching anything not listed.
